newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends higher on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends higher on shortcovering.

text.p: Spot gold in Hong Kong closed a shade firmer on Thursday compared to New York's previous close on shortcovering, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$342.90/343.40 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$342.70/343.20 close on Wednesday.
Some dealers were shortcovering in gold despite the rise in dollar/yen.
"Dealers covered their short positions because they were expecting the Japanese to sell, but it didn't materialise," said one dealer.
Traders reported selling interest on the upside, but said that the day's activity had been quiet.
"There was much less activity today than yesterday, no special big trades, but because it was so quiet, any buying or selling moved the market," one dealer at a local bank said.
Physical demand was said discouraging, but some traders noted that the Wednesday holiday in Singapore and Malaysia and Thursday's Indonesia holiday had slowed demand.
"Unless gold drops...to around $340 per ounce, there is no rush to buy," one trader said.
Gold was likely to test $338 per ounce, some traders said.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,171 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil, from its previous fix at -5.00
